title: GeoDrive: 3D Geometry-Informed Driving World Model with Precise Action Control

output_modality.value: Single-view video predicted from one reference frame along a user-given ego trajectory.

control_signal.value: User-specified ego-vehicle camera trajectory (R, T, f per step); optionally 2D bounding boxes of other vehicles for dynamic editing (needed in training).

control_mechanism.value: First-frame point cloud is rendered along the trajectory; rendered video is VAE-encoded, concatenated with noisy latent into a light condition encoder whose features, via zero-initialised linear layers, modulate a frozen DiT.

base_model.value: Frozen CogVideo-5B-I2V video diffusion transformer; condition encoder clones first two DiT layers (6% of parameters); MonST3R supplies 3D points and poses.

datasets.value: Trained on nuScenes (25,109 video-condition pairs); evaluated on nuScenes validation and zero-shot on a Waymo validation subset of 5 scenes.

metrics.value: LPIPS, PSNR, SSIM, FID, FVD for quality; ADE and FDE for action fidelity.

controllability_evidence.value: Trajectory following versus Vista on nuScenes: ADE x10^2 1.62 versus 2.77 and FDE x10^2 3.1 versus 5.28; the introduction states a 42% error reduction. Reverse trajectory is shown qualitatively.

closed_loop.value: No; open-loop generation along given trajectories. A VLA plan-and-verify use is shown only as a qualitative illustration.

stated_limitations.value: Depends on depth and pose accuracy from MonST3R; relies only on image and trajectory input. Static first-frame rendering is a limit addressed by dynamic editing.

notes: Table 1 data scale is listed as 5h for GeoDrive versus 1740h for Vista. Packet text includes NUL bytes in places but remained readable.
